sections.h2: 2. Weigh the warranty, not only the price
parts: Omega's warranties differ a lot by model. The Effortless and the Pure Press list a 15-year limited warranty on their product pages. The JC4000, the Time Saving batch juicer and the High Speed juicer list 1 year (12 months).

So the $399.99 Pure Press costs about $27 a year over its warranty, while the $134.99 JC4000 is covered for one year. If you juice every day and plan to keep the machine, the longer warranty can be the cheaper choice over time.

sections.h2: 3. Pick the type of juicer you'll actually use
parts: Omega sells three kinds of juicer. The High Speed juicer ($109.99) is a 1,000-watt centrifugal model with a 3.3-inch chute: the cheapest and fastest. The JC4000 ($134.99) and the Pure Press ($399.99) are vertical slow juicers; the JC4000 turns at 50 to 75 RPM and has a 3-inch mouth. The two batch juicers, the Time Saving ($159.99) and the Effortless ($499.99 and up), take a whole recipe at once in a hopper; the Effortless hopper holds 2 liters (68 oz) and stops by itself after five minutes.
If you want a slow juicer on a budget, the JC4000 is the lowest price for one. If you want to load everything and walk away, the Time Saving batch juicer costs less than a third of the Effortless.
Choosing a model? Our [best Omega juicer guide](saving-tips-best-omega-juicer.html) compares all five on speed, warranty, ratings and price.

sections.h2: 4. Buy parts instead of a new juicer

Some screens and drums were sold out on November 14. If your juicer still runs, a part is far cheaper than a new machine, and the code works on parts too.
